name: Bristol Onion
grown_as: Round-headed leek, known locally as the Bristol onion: a perennial bulb, native in Britain only on the limestone of the Avon Gorge (and on Jersey). William's seed is from Bristol Botanic Garden. Also sold as the 'drumstick allium' for borders.
habit: A slender, upright plant: a few thin leaves from the bulb that are withering by flowering time, and one wiry stem 40 to 90 cm topped by a small tight head. Plants often in small groups from offset bulbs.

leaf.arrangement: Two to six from the bulb, their sheaths wrapping the lowest third of the flower stem
leaf.outline: Thin, half-round, 15 to 40 cm by 2 to 4 mm
leaf.base: A sheath round the lower stem
leaf.surface: Hollow, smooth, with a shallow groove along the upper side
leaf.colour: Grey-green; yellow and brown by flowering time

flower.form: A dense, egg-shaped to round head packed with small bell-shaped flowers
flower.petals: Six oval tepals forming a small upright bell
flower.colour: Deep red-purple to maroon; buds at the base of the head still green when the top is open, so a young head is two-toned
flower.centre: Six stamens sticking out beyond the tepals, with purple anthers
flower.behind: A short papery spathe of two valves, shorter than the head
flower.carried: One head of 40 to 100 or more flowers on short stalks at the top of a slender, smooth, upright stem; the head opens from the top downwards
flower.size: Flowers 4 to 5 mm; head 2 to 3.5 cm long

fruit: The head dries to a tight brown egg of papery three-lobed capsules with small black seeds. Some heads carry small bulbils among the flowers.
seedling: Not drawn: drawn from a bulb. (From seed: one thin grass-like leaf, taking two or three years to flower.)
winter: Thin grey-green leaves come up in autumn and stand through winter into spring. ⚠️ CHECK: Claude believes the leaves are winter-green, as in many Mediterranean alliums.

leaf: a thin half-round hollow leaf with a groove on the upper side
bloom: a dense egg-shaped head of small deep red-purple bells
set: a small round to egg-shaped bulb, 1 to 2 cm, with papery brown skin
small offset bulblets at its base
young: a few thin grey-green leaves from the bulb
flower: one slender upright stem with a small tight red-purple egg-shaped head
seedhead: a tight brown egg-shaped head of dry capsules on a straw-coloured stem
dormant: a few thin grey-green leaves at ground level

look_alikes: Wild onion (crow garlic, Allium vineale) has heads mostly of bulbils with a long spathe and few pinkish flowers. Wild leek (Allium ampeloprasum) is much larger with flat leaves and a big round pale head. Chives have pink-purple pompoms and fine hollow leaves, flowering earlier.
